tally.headline: 1 of 3 gradeable claims held up, 2 did not

implied_side.book: captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at DraftKings
implied_side.why: EdgeDesk’s own number sat 1.8 points toward Ohio State of the quote EdgeDesk captured at captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at DraftKings. That is what the disagreement implied. It was published as research, not as a recommendation to bet it.

implied_total.why: EdgeDesk published no fair total, or no sportsbook total was captured.

closing_line.why: no closing line is held for this game: the Collective captured none and the schedule feed carries none. Closing-line value is left blank rather than estimated from the result.

reasons: 1 of 1 gradeable claims held up and none was contradicted. The game was decided by the things EdgeDesk said would decide it.
EdgeDesk projected a away margin of 9.3 and the game finished 12 the home way — 21.3 points of margin error, OUTSIDE the range the model published.
process.basis: the drivers, matchups and measured advantages only — never the price or the market claim, which are the result in longer words

verdict.line: The number did not land and the reasoning did. That is the case a bettor should be least upset about: the read was defensible and the distribution went the other way. Nothing here needs changing yet.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 2 published claims said the same thing: EdgeDesk prices this game at USC +9.5 with a fair total of 51.0, which makes Ohio State the better team here by that margin on this field. EdgeDesk makes it USC +9.5 where the market has USC +7.5 at captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at DraftKings — a 1.8 points disagreement.
lessons.actual_result: Ohio State Buckeyes lost by 12 where EdgeDesk projected a 9.3-point edge. Ohio State Buckeyes lost by 12.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk named Ohio State as better in market and the game went the other way, across 2 separate published claims. One game does not overturn a season-long rating, but this is the direction to watch: USC Trojans won the game outright
lessons.suggested_investigation: These claims carried 11.1 points of the published number between them and were contradicted. Check whether the same category has been contradicted in other games this season before touching anything.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 9 of the claims in this article rested on model, passing, rushing, matchup.
lessons.actual_result: None of them could be graded: no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes this driver; the read does not name a side, so there is no direction to test.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk prices these games partly on signals it has no way to observe afterwards. That is not an error in the model — it is a gap in the audit, and it means the platform cannot tell, from results alone, whether those parts of the number are earning their weight.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Consider whether a postgame data source exists for model, passing, rushing.

lessons.actual_result: It graded a loss, and the reasoning held up: 1 of 1 gradeable claims held up and none was contradicted. The game was decided by the things EdgeDesk said would decide it.
lessons.lesson: A losing number on a read the game supported. This is the result type that should change the least. Over-correcting on it is how a defensible process gets thrown away for a distribution doing what distributions do.

lessons.pregame_expectation: The model published an outcome range of -30.3 → +11.7 (USC).
lessons.actual_result: The game finished outside it, at a margin of 12.
lessons.lesson: The published range is meant to contain eight results in ten. A miss is expected roughly twice in ten games and is only a problem in aggregate — which is exactly what this store exists to measure.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Count range misses across the season. A rate materially above 20% means the model’s stated uncertainty is too narrow.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk makes it USC +9.5 where the market has USC +7.5 at captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at DraftKings — a 1.8 points disagreement.
lessons.actual_result: Ohio State Buckeyes lost by 12. the result landed on the market’s side of the disagreement
lessons.lesson: The market had the better estimate here. EdgeDesk’s disagreement was not information on this game, and the honest reading is that the price already contained what the model thought it had found.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Track disagreements of this size across the season. The question is not whether one landed; it is whether the class of them has any edge at all.
